setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dancing In The Street** (3 reviews): The strangest moment of the show, with vocals and playing at their most skewed; Bobby's vocals get very weird, even for him, and he makes Donna laugh at one point [8][10][16]
- **Supplication** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out Bobby's singing on Looks Like Rain and Supplication as outstanding; Reviewer calls the end of Supplication the best they have heard, with Weir playing ferociously [9][16]
- **Werewolves Of London** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls it a fine version of the song; Suited Jerry well and made a fun encore, showing the band having a ball [13][19]
- **Cold Rain And Snow** (1 review): Reviewer praises Jerry's fierce singing on this opening song [9]

## The recordings

- **gd78-05-11.moore.minches.18658.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 23 songs; 188 min; rated 3.92/5 by 13 [1]. Said about its sound: Nice audience recording with Garcia's voice front and center amid the cheering crowd [12]
- **gd1978-05-11.127386.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 174 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd1978-05-11.147804.2nd.Set.fob.shure.sm57.sublette.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 10 songs; 93 min [6]
- **gd78-05-11.sbd.miller.16333.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 166 min; rated 3.8/5 by 5 [3]

## Around the show

- Known as the mescaline show; tempos, vocals and details are slightly off throughout, with the oddness peaking in Dancing In The Street [8]
- Reviewer hears the band as heavily on psychedelics during the show, yet still playing fairly smoothly [11]
- Reviewer theorizes the band's weirdness and abilities came from consuming cannabis before and during the show [14]
- Reviewer prefers this audience tape to the other circulating audience source; finds 1978 spotty but this show nice [16]
- Reviewer says this audience tape is better than the other one available on the site [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd78-05-11.moore.minches.18658.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Moore, Maisner, and Spitalny; transferred by David Minches; source: Audience Recording: Nak 700's [1]. Also: Recorded by Moore, Maisner and Spitalny on Nak 700s to Nak 550 to Sony TC-152, from the floor right of center; Transferred from the cassette master by David Minches via Nak Dragon, ART DI/O, Waveterminal 2496, Cool Edit 2000 and mkwACT [1]
- **gd1978-05-11.127386.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: taped by dusborne; transferred by dusborne; source: 3 Source Matrix from Soundboard (shnid:16333), Audience (shnid:06317) and Audience (shnid:18658) [2]. Also: Front-of-board audience recording on Nak mics to Sony D5, cassette master, then DAT; transferred to CD and FLAC; Drums and space were mostly cut from the DAT; the missing drums section was patched from the circulating soundboard by Matt Vernon [2]
- **gd1978-05-11.147804.2nd.Set.fob.shure.sm57.sublette.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Kathy Sublette; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Kathy Sublette's Master (FOB) Audience Cassette; Shure SM57 mics > Sony-TC158 > Cassette [6]. Also: Second set comes from Kathy Sublette's backup cassette, transferred by Charlie Miller, because the master tapes were stolen; Weir's Lighting Engineer Rap and a 16:55 Drums > Space patch come from the shnid 18658 Nakamichi 700 source; A six-second patch in the Not Fade Away > Stella Blue transition comes from Matt Vernon's shnid 6317 Nakamichi 700 source [6]
- **gd78-05-11.sbd.miller.16333.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Springfield Civic Center Arena - May 11, 1978](https://www.dead.net/show/may-11-1978) [23]
